title: Special Order for Louisiana Public Service Commission, ex parte. — This Special Order ratifies votes taken by Commissioner Francis acting as the Commission’s representative on the Board of Directors of the Organization of MISO States.

documents.text:
LOUISIANA PUBLIC SERVICE COMMISSION
                            SPECIAL ORDER NUMBER 67-2026

                      LOUISIANA PUBLIC SERVICE COMMISSION
                                   EX PARTE

In re: This Special Order ratifies votes taken by Commissioner Francis acting as the
Commission’s representative on the Board of Directors of the Organization of MISO States.

              (Decided at the September 16, 2026 Business and Executive Session.)


                                             ORDER

I.     OVERVIEW

       This matter was on the agenda for ratification of a vote taken on August 13, 2026 by
Commissioner Francis as the LPSC’s representative on the Organization of MISO States ("OMS")
Board of Directors. Staff followed the protocols set forth in Special Order 17-2019 to consult
with the Executive Secretary and Chairman and to make a recommendation to Commissioner
Francis prior to the vote. The protocols also require that any votes taken be ratified at a following
B&E. The vote to be ratified is summarized as follows:

               At its August 13, 2026 board meeting, the OMS approved comments
               to be filed in FERC Docket No. EL26-70, MISO’s Resource
               Adequacy Informational Filing. FERC directed MISO to explain
               how it intends to ensure that adequate generation will be available
               to serve existing and new large loads. MISO made its filing and
               described how it works with the states to ensure adequate generation
               is in place, and it described its studies and processes to identify
               resource needs and accelerate interconnection.

               The OMS Comments expanded upon MISO’s filing by providing to
               FERC the retail regulator perspective, including how states have
               generation resource adequacy authority, how states balance
               provision of resource adequacy with affordability, and how states
               have been successful so far in making sure that the generation
               needed to serve large loads is provided timely without cost
               shifting. On Staff’s recommendation, Commissioner Francis voted
               in favor of the OMS pleading.


II.    COMMISSION JURISDICTION AND AUTHORITY

       The jurisdiction of the Commission is set forth by the Louisiana Constitution Article IV,
Section 21, which provides:

               The commission shall regulate all common carriers and public
               utilities and have such other regulatory authority as provided by law.
               It shall adopt and enforce reasonable rules, regulations, and
               procedures necessary for the discharge of its duties, and shall have
               other powers and perform other duties as provided by law.




                                                                        Special Order No. 67-2026
                                                                                           Page 1
 III.   CONCLUSION

       This matter was placed on the Commission’s September 16, 2026 B&E Agenda for
ratification by the full Commission. On motion of Chairman Skrmetta, seconded by Commissioner
Lewis, with Vice Chairman Coussan and Commissioner Campbell concurring, and Commissioner
Francis abstaining, the Commission voted to ratify the vote cast by Commissioner Francis as the
Louisiana Public Service Commission’s representative to the OMS Board of Directors.


This Order is effective immediately.


BY ORDER OF THE COMMISSION
BATON ROUGE, LOUISIANA
October 7, 2026
